reason: Both are rate-regulated utilities that deliver gas to residential and commercial customers. Con Edison is mainly an electric, gas and steam utility in NYC and Westchester. NJR is mainly a gas distributor in New Jersey, with a sizeable unregulated side: wholesale energy marketing, gas storage and pipelines, solar and home services. The gas distribution overlap is real. Electric and steam delivery are absent at NJR. The wholesale, storage and home services lines are absent at Con Edison. The service territories are different, so they don't compete for the same customers. Customer type is similar, but the actual customers are not shared. That makes it adjacent rather than direct.
